name: Low poly
plain: Pictures built from many small flat triangles, like a cut gem.
origin: Hardware-limited 3D games of the mid 1990s, taken up as a deliberate art style around late 2013 [S1]
defining: Surfaces broken into small flat polygons placed side by side, giving an angular, minimal look [S2]
Few polygons on purpose: a reference elephant uses 346 triangles against 1.89 million in the detailed version [S1]
Each facet usually holds one flat colour, so light steps from face to face rather than blending [inferred]
A drawn or rendered asset (illustration or 3D). Interface tokens can only echo it with sharp corners, clipped polygon shapes and two-tone fills
fits: Game sites, outdoor and tech brand heroes, posters, wallpapers and onboarding scenes.
goes_wrong: Auto-triangulated photo filters that look like dated stock backgrounds.
accessibility: Busy facets behind text drop contrast: keep text on solid panels at 4.5:1 and stop rotating 3D scenes under reduced motion.

sources.supports: Definition, 1990s console origin, deliberate style from late 2013, 346 vs 1.89 million triangle example, Mirror Moon EP
Simple geometric shapes side by side, angular minimalist look, render-time origin, 2,520-polygon portrait, use by illustrators and 3D artists

examples.name: Mirror Moon EP (game, 2013)
examples.what: Cited as the oldest Steam title tagged low poly, an early deliberate use of the style

name: Voxel art
plain: Scenes built from tiny coloured cubes, like digital LEGO.
origin: 1990s video game production, kept alive by retro-styled games and art [S1]
defining: Every form is built from equal coloured cubes; detail depends on cube count, from about ten for a crude house to thousands [S1]
The 3D cousin of pixel art: each voxel is one value on a regular 3D grid [S2]
Usually shown as small dioramas from a fixed three-quarter angle with soft rendered light [inferred]
A rendered 3D asset made in editors such as MagicaVoxel or Qubicle [S1]. Tokens can only echo it with square corners and stepped, unblurred shadows
fits: Games, kids' learning and maker products, playful heroes, empty states and 404 pages.
goes_wrong: Reads as a Minecraft copy, or the cube grid is too coarse to show the subject.
accessibility: Scenes are decorative: give them a short text description or empty alt text, and stop spinning dioramas under reduced motion.

sources.supports: Definition as coloured 3D boxes, cube counts, 1990s game origin, LEGO comparison, MagicaVoxel and Qubicle, Minecraft and Crossy Road
Voxel as a value on a regular 3D grid akin to a pixel; voxel art as a style analogous to pixel art

examples.name: Minecraft
examples.what: Named as a voxel-style game; its whole world is drawn as cubes

examples.name: Crossy Road
examples.what: Named as a game using the retro voxel look

name: Layered paper cut
plain: Shapes cut from coloured paper, stacked so each layer casts shadow.
origin: Papercutting began in China, oldest surviving piece 6th century [S2]; layered, photographed paper illustration grew in editorial and ad work [S1]
defining: Flat, matte colour shapes with crisp cut edges, made by hand and photographed [S1]
Depth from stacking: makers lift layers on foam board so each casts a small soft shadow [S3]
Soft lighting and shadows define the form, often leaving clear space for copy [S1]
The craft piece or a 3D render is the asset. In UI, tokens can carry it as flat fills plus two to four small stacked soft shadows [inferred]
fits: Editorial covers, children's and education brands, seasonal campaigns, onboarding and empty-state scenes.
goes_wrong: Shadows too dark or too many layers, so it turns muddy instead of crisp.
accessibility: Layer shadows are decorative: text still needs 4.5:1 on the paper colour, and parallax layers should stop under reduced motion.

sources.supports: Folded, laser-cut and layered paper in contemporary design; photographed paper leaves with space for copy; soft light and shadow; Hattie Newman for Canon; Zim & Zou for Hermes
Chinese origin and 6th-century oldest surviving example; jianzhi, papel picado, scherenschnitte, kirigami traditions
Owen Gildersleeve raises paper layers with foam board to add depth; tactile illustration defined

examples.what: A detailed paper city built for a Canon expo

name: Stained glass
plain: Bright see-through colour pieces joined by thick dark lines.
origin: European churches and cathedrals, at its height between 1150 and 1550 [S1]
defining: Colour sits in the glass itself, tinted with metal oxides, so hues glow when lit from behind [S1][S2]
Pieces are held in H-shaped lead strips (cames) whose dark lines are part of the design [S1]
Drawn from a full-size cartoon; faces and shading painted in grey-black vitreous paint and fired on [S1][S3]
An illustration or pattern asset. In UI, tokens can carry only the thick dark outline, saturated fills and a back-lit glow [inferred]
code: border: 4px solid #1b1b1f; background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 30%, #ffd166, #e63946 70%); filter: saturate(1.2);
fits: Heritage, church and cultural brands, fantasy games, posters, book covers and seasonal illustration.
goes_wrong: Black lead lines everywhere make a heavy, busy page that crowds out text.
accessibility: Vivid back-lit colour behind text fails easily: put text on a solid panel at 4.5:1 and never rely on hue alone.

sources.supports: 1150 to 1550 peak, metallic oxides colour the glass, vitreous paint, H-shaped lead cames as an integral part of the design
Glass coloured by metallic salts, pieces held by lead cames in a rigid frame
Making steps: full-size cartoon, cutting coloured glass, enamel painting, leading

name: Watercolour
plain: Soft see-through paint that bleeds and pools on paper.
origin: A continuous art medium from the Renaissance, matured in 18th and 19th century England [S2]; a recurring logo, web and packaging trend [S1]
defining: Colour bleeds into the page and into neighbouring colours [S1]
Transparent layers let the paper and lower layers show through [S2]
Visible texture and imperfect-on-purpose edges and splotches [S1]
Blends of three colours or fewer, or they turn muddy [S1]
A painted or scanned image asset. Tokens carry only the paper-white ground, soft tints and an optional texture image
fits: Wellness, food and drink, weddings, children's books, stationery and gentle brand accents.
goes_wrong: Too many colours blended into brown mud, or paint placed behind body text.
accessibility: Washes are low contrast: never set text over them without a solid backing that holds 4.5:1.

sources.supports: Watercolour as a design trend; colour bleed, texture, imperfect-on-purpose feel; three colours or fewer advice; use as an accent in logos
Renaissance continuity, English watercolour school, transparency and glazing layers, washes

name: Chalkboard
plain: White chalk writing and doodles on a dark green or black board.
origin: Classroom slate boards; the word chalkboard came with green enamel boards from 1930 [S2]; revived as retro hand-lettered signage by letterers such as Dana Tanamachi [S1]
defining: Matte dark ground, usually black or dark green, with white or coloured chalk marks [S2]
Retro hand lettering mixed with doodles, banners and borders [S1]
Dusty, uneven strokes with smudges and eraser haze [inferred]
Lettering and texture are drawn assets. Tokens carry the dark matte surface, off-white text and a faint noise texture
fits: Cafes, bakeries, bars and restaurant menus, teaching products, hand-made event signs.
goes_wrong: Long text set in chalk fonts, which becomes hard to read at small sizes.
accessibility: Off-white on dark passes easily, but rough chalk fonts hurt legibility: keep body text in a plain face and use chalk for headings only.

sources.supports: Dana Tanamachi's chalk lettering blending retro typography and craft; window displays for Rugby Ralph Lauren, work for Ace Hotel
Dark matte black or green boards, green enamel from 1930 and the word chalkboard, A-frame boards for restaurant and bar specials

examples.name: Rugby Ralph Lauren window displays by Dana Tanamachi
examples.what: Chalk type recalling 1940s signage, drawn on store windows

name: Blueprint
plain: White line drawings on a deep blue sheet, often with a grid.
origin: Cyanotype process found by Sir John Herschel in 1842, used to copy technical drawings until diazo prints took over from the 1940s [S1][S2]
defining: Prussian-blue ground with white negative lines [S1][S2]
One colour only: blue, white and tints between them [S2]
Thin, even technical lines, often over a fine square grid [inferred]
Plans and diagrams are drawn assets, but tokens carry the rest in UI: blue surface, white hairline borders and a CSS grid background
fits: Architecture, engineering, hardware and developer tools, launches that explain how something is built.
goes_wrong: Hairlines too faint on blue, or a cliche when nothing is actually being explained.
accessibility: White on deep blue is high contrast, but faint grid lines and thin type can fall below 3:1: keep text solid white and treat the grid as decoration.

sources.supports: Contact print of technical drawings, Herschel 1842, white-on-blue from cyanotype, diazo whiteprints from the early 1940s
Cyanotype 1842, Prussian blue, white negative images, monochromatic blue and white

examples.name: Anna Atkins cyanotype botanical studies (1854), V&A
examples.what: White plant silhouettes on Prussian blue, the root of the blueprint look

name: Technical drawing
plain: Precise thin black lines, measurements, labels and tiny data notes.
origin: Drafting conventions codified in standards such as ISO 128 [S1]; named as a branding trend for 2026 [S2]
defining: Shared conventions for line styles, symbols, lettering and page layout make drawings unambiguous [S1]
Orthographic views, cross sections and dimension lines [S1]
Tight type overlays, grids, timestamps and tiny metrics used as texture [S2]
Mostly carried by tokens: hairline borders, mono or condensed caps, numbered labels and a strict grid. Diagrams themselves are assets
code: border: 1px solid #111; font: 500 11px/1.3 ui-monospace, monospace; letter-spacing: .04em; text-transform: uppercase;
fits: Hardware, sportswear and performance brands, developer tools, data products and spec pages.
goes_wrong: Fake data and decorative numbers that mean nothing, set too small to read.
accessibility: Micro labels often drop under 12px and hairlines under 3:1: keep real text at body size and 4.5:1, and treat tiny marks as decoration.

sources.supports: Visual language of symbols, line styles and layout; ISO 128; orthographic and section views
The aesthetics of technical information as a 2026 trend: diagrams, metrics, grids, timestamps; Astrae Studio for Nike

examples.name: Astrae Studio campaigns for Nike and Astrae Sports
examples.what: Grids and technical symbols used as page furniture

name: Liquid metal
plain: Shiny melted silver, like mirror chrome poured into letters.
origin: Grew from metal-music lettering and acid graphics into youth-culture branding [S1]; back in tech launches in 2025 [S2]
defining: Gleaming 3D surfaces with sharp mirror reflections and a computerised feel [S1]
Sinuous, dripping or plumped letterforms [S1]
Often animated as flowing reflections, tuned by refraction and speed [S2]
Made with 3D rendering or shaders, so it is an asset. Tokens can only fake a still version with a steep grey gradient clipped to text
code: background: linear-gradient(180deg, #fff 0%, #a7b0ba 45%, #2b2f36 52%, #d9dee3 100%); -webkit-background-clip: text; background-clip: text; color: transparent;
fits: Music, fashion, sneaker and youth-culture launches, product event invites and logo moments.
goes_wrong: Melted type nobody can read, and a dated cliche when used on everything.
accessibility: Reflections swing from white to near black so parts of letters vanish: keep a solid fallback colour, real text for screen readers, and stop the flow under reduced motion.

sources.supports: Names (liquid metal, chromic graphics, chrometype), gleaming 3D type, computerised look, metal-scene and acid-graphics roots, Dazed beauty identity
Paper's open-source liquid-metal logo tool (February 2025), inspired by Apple event invites; refraction and speed controls

name: Holographic foil
plain: Shiny rainbow surface that changes colour as it tilts.
origin: Packaging foil finish that went mainstream in the late 2010s [S1][S2]
defining: Colour shifts through pink, green and blue as the light moves [S3]
Usually set against black or white grounds with simple graphics [S2]
Used as a foil-stamped accent or a full-pack wrap [S1][S3]
A physical finish or an animated render. In UI, tokens can only imitate it with a multi-stop pastel gradient on small accents, ideally moving with the pointer
fits: Beauty, drinks, fashion and music packaging, collectible cards and small premium accents.
goes_wrong: Whole surfaces in rainbow sheen with pale text on top, which looks cheap and is unreadable.
accessibility: Pastel sheen gives low contrast: keep text on solid black or white, and stop tilt shimmer under reduced motion.

sources.supports: Holographic foil and iridescent finishes becoming mainstream in packaging
Holographic effects on black or white backgrounds as a 2020 packaging trend; shiny multi-coloured metallics
Lumee pouch shifting through pink, green and blue; foil-stamped wordmark

name: Neon sign
plain: Glowing coloured tube letters lighting up a dark wall.
origin: Georges Claude's neon tubes, first shown at the Paris Motor Show in December 1910 [S1]
defining: Single continuous tube lines bent into letters or pictures, glowing on a dark ground [S1]
A bright white core with wider coloured halos, built from several stacked shadows [S2]
True neon glows reddish orange; other colours come from other gases and coatings [S1]
Optional flicker where the glow drops out in quick flashes [S2]
Carried by tokens: dark surface plus text-shadow or box-shadow glow. Bent-tube lettering is a typeface or drawn asset
fits: Bars, nightlife, music and gaming events, night-mode accents and sign-style headings.
goes_wrong: Glow so wide the letters blur, and fast flicker on every element.
accessibility: Halos blur edges and flicker can trigger seizures: keep the core text solid at 4.5:1, never flash more than three times a second, and remove flicker under reduced motion.

sources.supports: Georges Claude, Paris Motor Show December 1910; reddish-orange true neon; other colours from gases and phosphor coatings; bent glass tubes
Stacked text-shadow glow with a white inner glow and wider coloured glow; flicker keyframes

name: Letterpress
plain: Ink letters pressed into thick soft paper, leaving a dent.
origin: Gutenberg's movable type, about 1440; revived as a craft with visible impression from the 1990s [S1]
defining: Type and art pressed into the stock so they sit below the surface [S1]
Deep bite was a printing fault before the revival; now it is the point [S2]
Crisper type than offset because of the impression [S1]
Usually one or two spot inks on thick, soft paper [inferred]
In UI, tokens carry it: an inset look from a light 1px highlight below and a faint dark edge above on text, inputs or wells
fits: Stationery, weddings, invitations, premium packaging and quiet luxury brand touches.
goes_wrong: Fake inset shadows on grey-on-grey text so words look washed out.
accessibility: Debossed text is often grey on grey: keep the ink colour at 4.5:1 against the paper and never rely on the shadow to show the letter.

sources.supports: Relief printing; Gutenberg about 1440; revival with deep impression; Martha Stewart Weddings in the 1990s; crisper than offset; debossed output
Tactile impression was once considered bad printing; today linked with wedding invitations and stationery

name: Woodcut and linocut
plain: Bold carved-looking prints with rough black shapes and white cut lines.
origin: Woodcut in Europe from about 1400, after older Chinese woodblock printing [S1]; linocut popularised in Britain from 1919 [S2]
defining: Cut-away areas stay paper-white while the raised surface carries ink [S1][S2]
Cutting simplifies drawing into strong, simple graphic shapes with a limited palette [S2]
Often one or two inks; one-colour posters are common [S2][S3]
Gouge marks and pattern stand in for shading [inferred]
A printed or drawn asset. Tokens carry only the ink and paper colours, sharp edges and a print texture
fits: Craft food and drink, book covers, cinema and festival posters, folk and outdoor brands.
goes_wrong: Digital fakes with smooth, even vector lines that lose the carved roughness.
accessibility: Fine cut lines vanish at small sizes: use the look for large images and keep body text in solid ink at 4.5:1.

sources.supports: Relief technique where cut-away areas carry no ink; Chinese origins; European woodcut from about 1400; Expressionist use
Linocut as woodcut on linoleum; simplifies style into strong graphic work and limited palettes; Claude Flight and Edith Lawrence from 1919; one-colour and black and white examples
Peter Strausfeld's linocut cinema posters with wood type, editions of about 300

name: Sumi-e ink brush
plain: Black ink brush strokes, from dark to pale grey, much empty paper.
origin: Tang dynasty China (618 to 907), carried on in Korea and Japan [S1]
defining: Usually monochrome: only shades of black ink [S1]
Tone comes from ink density and pressure within one stroke, from heavy and wet to light and dry [S1][S2]
Few strokes, each carrying meaning, with empty paper as part of the picture [inferred]
Brushwork is an asset. Tokens carry the warm paper ground, black ink text and generous empty space
fits: Tea, spa, wellness and meditation brands, East Asian cuisine, book covers and calm editorial.
goes_wrong: Used as generic 'Asian' decoration with fake calligraphy, which reads as careless or disrespectful.
accessibility: Pale grey washes fail contrast: keep text in full black at 4.5:1 and treat strokes as decoration.

sources.supports: Tang dynasty origin, monochrome black ink, tone from ink density and pressure, Japanese term sumie
Sumi ink from compressed charcoal; strokes from heavy and wet to light and dry; enso circle in Zen practice

name: Naive crayon drawing
plain: Wobbly drawings that look made by a child with crayons.
origin: Branding and illustration trend tracked from 2019 to 2026 as a reaction to polish and AI imagery [S1][S2]
defining: Rough, wobbly lines with visible crayon or pastel texture [S1][S3]
Bulbous, joyful figures and bright block colours [S3]
Minimal, intentional palettes, often set beside clean digital type [S1]
Frame-by-frame motion that exaggerates the roughness [S1]
Drawn assets carry it. Tokens add only slightly irregular corners, thick outlines and paper colours
fits: Bakeries, cafes, kids' and family brands, charities, music and culture campaigns, friendly onboarding.
goes_wrong: Looks careless rather than charming when the type and layout are messy too.
accessibility: Hand lettering and crayon text are hard to read: keep body text in a clear font at 4.5:1 and use drawings as decoration.

sources.supports: Childlike, naive, imperfect illustration as the 2026 trend; minimal palettes; rough illustration with clean type; frame-by-frame motion; Jolene Bakery and Little Wolf Coffee
Rise of childlike, crayon-covered graphics in 2024; Jolene logo drawn by a six-year-old in 2019
Crayon and pastel work, bulbous joyful figures, radiant block colours

name: Dithering and 1-bit
plain: Pictures made from scattered black and white dots, like old computer screens.
origin: Image dithering for limited displays from the early 1960s [S1]; chosen as a look by indie games and low-energy websites in the 2010s [S1][S2]
defining: Grey levels faked by the density of black and white dots [S1]
Patterns are either regular (ordered) or noisy (error diffusion, such as Floyd-Steinberg, 1975) [S1]
Low-tech Magazine reduces images to black, white and four greys, then tints them by section, for about ten times less data [S2]
Differs from pixel-art: the source is a photo or render reduced by an algorithm, not hand-placed sprites [inferred]
An image treatment. UI tokens carry the 1-bit palette, a tint colour and crisp, unsmoothed scaling [S3]
code: image-rendering: pixelated; filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.4); mix-blend-mode: multiply;
fits: Low-energy and sustainability sites, indie games, zines, music, retro-tech and editorial photo treatment.
goes_wrong: Faces and detail turn to noise, and dots scaled by odd amounts blur into grey mush.
accessibility: Dithered photos lose detail: give real alt text, keep text out of images, and scale by whole numbers so dots stay crisp.

sources.supports: Dot density for grey levels, 1-bit history, ordered and error-diffusion dithering, Floyd-Steinberg 1975, video game aesthetic and Return of the Obra Dinn
Images converted to black and white with four greys, coloured per category in the browser, about ten times less resource-intensive
image-rendering: pixelated for crisp scaling

examples.what: All photos dithered and tinted to cut page weight

examples.what: A modern game built on a 1-bit dithered look

name: Sketchy wireframe
plain: Interface drawn with wobbly pen lines, like a quick whiteboard sketch.
origin: Low-fidelity wireframing tools such as Balsamiq and hand-drawn drawing libraries such as Rough.js and Excalidraw [S1][S2][S3]
defining: Wobbly, slightly doubled strokes with an adjustable roughness setting [S2]
Deliberately unfinished and forgiving of alignment, so feedback stays on flow and content [S1]
Hand-drawn font and mostly greyscale fills with one accent [inferred]
Fully carried by code: a small library (under 9 kB gzipped) draws rough boxes, lines and fills in canvas or SVG [S2]
fits: Whiteboards, diagram and planning tools, early prototypes, explainers and docs that should feel provisional.
goes_wrong: Sloppy layout hiding behind the sketch excuse, or used for a finished product that must feel trustworthy.
accessibility: Handwriting fonts and jittery lines slow reading: offer a clean font option, keep text at 4.5:1 and strokes at 3:1.

sources.supports: Sketch style is forgiving about alignment and keeps focus on what matters; Clean style as the alternative
Library under 9 kB gzipped for sketchy, hand-drawn graphics in canvas and SVG; roughness option
Open-source virtual whiteboard with a hand-drawn style for diagrams and wireframes

name: Newsprint
plain: Cheap grey paper, black ink columns, halftone photos and big headlines.
origin: Cheap mechanical-pulp paper made for newspapers [S1]; newsprint-inspired branding and faked print effects in the 2020s [S2][S3]
defining: Low-cost paper that yellows and turns brittle in air and sunlight [S1]
Scratchy, inky texture in black, white and one spot colour such as red [S2]
Desaturated halftone photos treated like cut-outs [S3]
Dense multi-column text under large headlines [inferred]
Mostly carried by tokens: off-white surface, black serif text, columns and rules. Ink texture and halftone are image assets
code: background: #eceae4; color: #1a1a1a; columns: 3 16rem; column-rule: 1px solid #1a1a1a; font-family: Georgia, serif;
fits: Newsletters, blogs and media sites, food and drink labels, campaigns that want urgency or a press feel.
goes_wrong: Grey on grey with fake texture laid over body text.
accessibility: Grey paper lowers contrast: keep text near black for at least 4.5:1, keep line length readable, and drop to one column on phones.

sources.supports: Low-cost paper from mechanical pulp; lignin makes it yellow and brittle
Newsprint-inspired branding for Braxton Brewing by Durham Brand & Co.: scratchy inky texture, black, white and red
Halftone and desaturated print effects that make images look like newspaper cut-outs

name: Felt and embroidery
plain: Pictures made from soft cut felt or colourful stitched thread.
origin: Felt is one of the oldest known textiles [S3]; felt and thread became tactile illustration media in editorial and ad work [S1][S2]
defining: Felt shapes cut from stencils in flat colours; cut felt spreads slightly past the drawn outline [S1]
Embroidery layers colour stitch by stitch, and different stitches mimic different textures [S1][S2]
Pieces are photographed so fibres and small imperfections show [S1]
Craft or rendered assets carry it. Tokens add only warm fills, soft rounded corners and an inset dashed 'stitch' outline
fits: Children's brands, crafts and homeware, cosy seasonal campaigns, stop-motion animation and editorial covers.
goes_wrong: Cheap digital stitch filters that look fake, or fabric texture behind text.
accessibility: Fabric textures behind text lower contrast: keep text on flat colour at 4.5:1 and pause stop-motion loops under reduced motion.

sources.supports: Tactile illustration with paper, embroidery and fabric; Jacopo Rosatti's stencil-cut felt and its spreading edges; stitches simulate textures; photography
Maricor/Maricar embroidered lettering; layering colour; tactile, warm medium; Vogue Japan work
Felt as matted, pressed fibres and one of the oldest known textiles; revival in fibre arts from the 1970s

name: Marbling
plain: Swirly veined colour patterns, like floating ink or polished marble.
origin: Floated-colour paper decoration known from Turkey; made in Europe from the early 17th century for bookbinding [S1]
defining: Colours floated on a liquid bath, then stirred or combed into waves, veins and comb patterns [S1]
Patterns range from calm to busy depending on how strong and frequent the swirls are [S2]
One colour reads classic; many shades read lively [S2]
A texture or pattern asset. Tokens only place it as a background image or border fill behind solid panels
code: background: #f4efe8 url(marble.jpg) center / cover; background-blend-mode: multiply;
fits: Book covers and endpapers, stationery, chocolate and cosmetics packaging, hospitality and luxury backgrounds.
goes_wrong: Stock marble photos as page backgrounds that look like a bathroom counter.
accessibility: Busy veins break up letter shapes: keep text on a solid band at 4.5:1.

sources.supports: Paints floated on liquid and paper laid on top; 1627 account of the Turkish art; early 17th-century German start; French link to bookbinding; combed and nonpareil patterns

name: Cel-shaded
plain: 3D characters shaded like a cartoon, with hard light and dark steps.
origin: Non-photorealistic rendering in games; Jet Set Radio drew attention to it when shown in 1999 [S1]
defining: Smooth lighting cut into a few flat shade bands, so shadows read as blocks of colour [S1]
Black ink outlines on silhouettes and contours [S1]
Typically a base colour plus first and second shade colours, with an adjustable soft edge between them [S2]
A rendered 3D asset. UI can echo it with unblurred offset shadows, solid outlines and two-step fills
fits: Games, anime and animation, toys, youth brands, mascots and launch trailers.
goes_wrong: Poor silhouettes: the flat look exposes every modelling error.
accessibility: Hard outlines help clarity, but keep text off busy scenes at 4.5:1 and pause character motion under reduced motion.

sources.supports: Definition as NPR, quantised discrete shades, black ink outlines, Jet Set Radio 1999, The Wind Waker and other games

name: Monoline line art
plain: Drawings made from one even-thickness line, with no fills.
origin: Stroke-based icon systems and single-line logo art in digital brands [S1][S2]
defining: One stroke width everywhere: Lucide uses 2 px strokes on a 24 x 24 px canvas with 1 px padding [S1]
Round caps and joins, with almost every sharp corner rounded [S1]
Continuous single-line versions reduce a mark to its key gestures [S2]
Fully carried by tokens in UI: stroke width, cap and join, icon size and current text colour
code: fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 2; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round;
fits: Icon systems, product UI, wellness and lifestyle logos, spot illustrations and packaging marks.
goes_wrong: Mixed stroke widths, or lines so thin they disappear at small sizes.
accessibility: Icon strokes need 3:1 against the background, and icon-only buttons need text labels.
